_comment: Phase 0 column orientation: SYNTHETIC cases run by BOTH copies of the algorithm (web/src/lib/orientation.test.ts and api/src/__tests__/orientation.test.ts). orientation = the web direction (W) / long side (HSS rect) / a side (HSS square), degrees counter-clockwise on screen from +X. A diamond is a 30 in square turned 45 degrees (a plate / pier) drawn around the column and used as the capture box: the reading must follow the column, never the diamond. Kind w3 is a W drawn as THREE strokes (two flanges and a web joined T-fashion), the way a real plan draws it; diamondSide is the diamond's side in inches (the real plate is about 21 in a side, 30 in across); centrelines adds two long lines along the page axes through the column centre (drawn over the web). Phase 0 fixes: diamondSide 16 is a plate whose box (22.6 in) fits under the family cap (23 in) yet still holds the W; neighbour adds a two-line HSS pair 8 to 15 in from the column (an 8 x 4 in HSS stood 5 pt from a column on the real page). Kind w3s is a W8 (8 x 8 in) drawn as three strokes: a W12X53 in a 16 in diamond would touch its edges (its corners are 0.1 pt from them), so the plate-below-the-cap cases use the smaller W.
